# Audit 03 — Potential for Future Expandability

**Audit date:** 2026-09-29 · **Reviewed commit:** `0564118` (main) · **Deployed:** `v1.0.0` (`a00803b`).

Scope: module boundaries, replaceable adapters, explicit contracts, data ownership and coupling; concrete obstacles to plausible future changes. The documented requirement that any new source must have authorized access ([portfolio.md](../portfolio.md#future-source-boundary)) is respected; no adapter, framework or abstraction was implemented or is recommended speculatively.

## Confirmed defects

None. Expandability issues below are structural observations, not functional defects.

## Missing verification

None applicable — this area is assessed by reading code and documentation.

## Accepted limitations (documented)

| ID     | Location                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Observation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| EXP-A1 | [OpportunityEmailParser.php](../../../app/Domain/Opportunities/Contracts/OpportunityEmailParser.php), [ParsedOpportunity.php](../../../app/Domain/Opportunities/Data/ParsedOpportunity.php), [config/opportunity_sources.php](../../../config/opportunity_sources.php) | The provider boundary is e-mail specific (`parse(string $rawEmail)`, `sourceMessageId`, MIME/sender assumptions, single Upwork configuration block). `OpportunityProvider` has one case. The portfolio guide states this honestly and lists the prerequisites (authorization, provider+external ID, provenance, no-network contract tests) for a separate ADR before any API source. |
| EXP-A2 | [ImportOpportunityEmail.php](../../../app/Application/Opportunities/ImportOpportunityEmail.php)                                                                                                                                                                        | Idempotency is keyed on `Message-ID` and raw-content SHA-256 — identities that only exist for e-mail. A non-e-mail source would need its own dedup identity and its own import action rather than reusing `email_imports`.                                                                                                                                                           |
| EXP-A3 | [OpportunityScorer.php](../../../app/Domain/Triage/OpportunityScorer.php), [TriageInput.php](../../../app/Domain/Triage/Data/TriageInput.php)                                                                                                                          | Four fixed rules and a fixed seven-key input snapshot; `engine_version = triage-v1` is a constant. Adding a rule changes the input contract, the profile schema (`weights` must sum to 100), `ENGINE_VERSION`, and makes all stored evaluations "UNSCORED" under the new engine. This is the intended immutability design (ADR-005) — expansion cost is deliberate, not accidental.  |
| EXP-A4 | `users.workspace_id` (single nullable FK)                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | One workspace per web user; multi-workspace membership would require a pivot and a workspace switcher. Tenant-ready schema (every table carries `workspace_id`) but single-assignment UI, as the roadmap states.                                                                                                                                                                     |

Any non-HTTP caller (CLI, future job) would receive HTTP-flavoured exceptions. `RecordOpportunityReview` already branches on `$dashboardDetails !== null` to choose between `TriageException` and HTTP exceptions, which is the seam where this coupling shows.                                                                                                               | Introduce one `StaleReviewContextException` (domain) and map it to 409 in `bootstrap/app.php`; keep the HTTP mapping where it is. Behavioural drift between the two implementations was already the subject of a post-completion correction (project sheet, Phase 4). | Keep both (read vs. locked write are legitimately different) but move the shared SQL fragments into named constants/methods on `ListReviewOpportunities` so a future change edits one place.                      |

Adding a reason code touches three files.                                                                          | Expose the allowed values from `RecordOpportunityReview::REASON_CODES`/`OUTCOMES` in the FormRequest rules, and ship them to the UI via the existing detail payload (`demo` block already carries server config). |

A minor `webklex/php-imap` upgrade can break it silently; the fake-protocol unit tests will catch signature changes but not behavioural ones.                                                                                                                                                  | Pin `webklex/php-imap` to an exact minor in `composer.json` and treat Dependabot bumps of it as requiring the target-host compatibility check from ADR-004.                                                       |

Per-workspace profiles would need a `workspaces.profile_path` (or stored profile) and a change to `LocalScoringProfileLoader` call sites (7 controller/command sites all read `config('opportunity_review.profile_path')`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | If needed, add a `ResolveActiveProfile` service that the controllers inject instead of reading config in each method.                                                                                             |

Their decisions are implemented and partly described in the project sheet and portfolio guide, but a future contributor has no single place for the tenancy and parser-drift rationale.                                                                                                                                                          | Write short backfill ADRs only if a second contributor joins; otherwise record the gap here.                                                                                                                      |

## Verified strengths (PASS)

- Layering is consistent: `Domain` (pure, no Laravel except container-free enums/DTOs), `Application` (use-cases, transactions), `Infrastructure` (parser, IMAP, profile loader), `Http`/`Console` (boundaries). PHPStan level 5 passes across `app/` and `tests/`.
- Replaceable contracts are bound in one place ([AppServiceProvider.php](../../../app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php#L22-L31)): `OpportunityEmailParser`, `MailboxClient`, `MonotonicClock`; deterministic fakes exist for the last two ([tests/Support/Fakes](../../../tests/Support/Fakes)).
- Scoring is reproducible from stored `profile_snapshot` + `input_snapshot`; evaluations and enrichments are immutable at the model level ([OpportunityEvaluation.php](../../../app/Models/OpportunityEvaluation.php#L60-L72)).
- Data ownership is explicit: every domain table has `workspace_id` with cascade; child records resolve through their parent.
- Frontend is plain Vue SFCs mounted into Blade shells with a single `http.js`; no SPA router or store to migrate away from.

## Review limits

No prototype of an alternative source or scorer rule was attempted; assessments are based on reading the contracts and their call sites.
